title: Why some banks won't open your account under $10M
description: A bank that turns away million-dollar depositors because a million dollars isn't the threshold. Private banking exists for a tier of wealth most people never see — and the fee for admission is silence, not cash.

scenes.narration: Walk into this bank with a million dollars. They'll turn you away.
scenes.imagePrompt: Interior of a private bank reception desk in polished dark marble with hand-finished brass fittings, bright daylight from tall windows, a dark gold-leaf coffered ceiling in shadow filling the top third, no people, no signage

scenes.narration: Private banking here starts at a minimum most millionaires never reach.
scenes.imagePrompt: A private bank vault corridor lined with hand-rubbed walnut panelling, bright daylight falling from a hidden skylight onto a polished limestone floor, dark vaulted ceiling in shadow above, no people

scenes.narration: The entry threshold typically starts around ten million dollars in assets.
scenes.imagePrompt: Close view of a heavy brushed-stainless-steel private bank vault door with a brass locking wheel standing ajar, warm daylight spilling in from a corridor, dark stone archway in shadow filling the top third, no people

scenes.narration: Clients above that line pay a management fee near one percent a year.
scenes.imagePrompt: Private bank meeting room with a single book-matched marble table and hand-stitched leather chairs in bright daylight from floor-to-ceiling windows, dark walnut-panelled wall in shadow above, no people, no documents visible

scenes.narration: In exchange, a single banker handles everything: tax, property, even art purchases.
scenes.imagePrompt: Private banker's oiled mahogany desk with a hand-stitched leather portfolio and a brass fountain pen laid on the polished wood, bright daylight through a tall window, dark bookshelf wall in shadow filling the top third, no people

scenes.narration: That relationship alone can be worth over fifty thousand dollars a year in service.
scenes.imagePrompt: Elegant private bank lounge with a single velvet armchair beside a marble side table with brass inlay, bright daylight, dark walnut-panelled wall in shadow above, no people, no signage

scenes.narration: The money was never really the product. The access was.
scenes.imagePrompt: Private bank rooftop terrace with polished stone paving and a single outdoor seating area behind a brushed-steel railing, overlooking a city skyline in bright daylight, dark building silhouette in shadow filling the top third, no people

scenes.narration: So the account minimum was never really about the money in it. It was about who gets to call. Follow for more of these.
scenes.imagePrompt: Interior of an empty private bank lobby with a polished marble floor reflecting bright daylight from tall arched windows, a dark gold-leaf coffered ceiling in shadow filling the top third of frame, no people, no signage
